claims.text: Severe lattice distortion caused by large atomic-size mismatches is the primary mechanism governing yield strength and deformation behavior in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Lattice distortion strengthens these alloys by impeding dislocation glide.
NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 can serve as a single-phase, disordered solid-solution HEA with a uniform microstructure.
The comparison will use variants differing primarily in atomic-size mismatch while retaining similar phase stability and compositional complexity.
Larger differences in constituent atomic radii produce greater lattice distortion.
Mechanical testing will span room temperature to approximately 1073 K under comparable strain-rate conditions.
Severe lattice distortion is associated with rugged dislocation lines and strongly variable dissociation widths.
The relevant local distortions and irregular dislocation configurations can be characterized by TEM and diffraction techniques.
Greater atomic-size mismatch creates an irregular local energy landscape that hinders dislocation glide.
Local heterogeneities impose larger barriers to dislocation motion and require higher flow stress.
Larger barriers to dislocation motion increase both yield strength and work hardening.
The high-mismatch variant will have statistically significantly greater yield strength and work hardening than the reduced-mismatch baseline.
The high-distortion variant will exhibit more rugged and non-uniform dislocation structures than the baseline.
The lattice-distortion mechanism should dominate in single-phase solid solutions when dislocation glide is the primary plasticity carrier, from room temperature to about 1073 K.
The proposed mechanism may cease to dominate when secondary phases form or when diffusion or twinning controls deformation.
Processing conditions may alter the quantitative mechanical response.
Short-range ordering may make a secondary contribution to strength even if it does not fundamentally change the activated plastic mechanisms.
Failure to observe a statistically significant strength and work-hardening increase, or failure to observe the predicted dislocation irregularity, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
